title: the proof standard's classes and its written conclusion
line: a household's census and a birth register read by data/evidence-classes.csv: the census a derivative whose birth is secondary information and indirect evidence (an age worked into a year), its residence primary, its parents a relationship FamilySearch computed; the birth register's own birth primary and direct, each record named by the original it was copied from; tools/proof.py writes the conclusion per key fact: the father's sex meets the standard, his birth owes an argument while its birthplace conflict is open (printed with its question id and the rule's own reading of it: the register states the birth first-hand, but its place is not yet resolved, so the rule would not decide it yet), his son's parents owe one on secondary information alone, the census stating him the head's son, his wife's birth, an age on the census worked into a year, owes one on indirect evidence and secondary information, and her marriage, which only the census's own grouping gives, rests on the file's claim the owner accepted, the grouping left undecided, and the home person's grandmother's, which her obituary states (the page the archive holds, read in the model's place and read as an obituary through the collection it is filed under), owes one on secondary information; the birthplace conflict closed by the owner with a written reason leaves only the research
